The Runge--Kutta method \cref{eq:RK} is called AS-stable if $I - z A$ is non-singular for all $z \in \C^-$ and $z b^T (I - z A)^{-1}$ is uniformly bounded for $z \in \C^-$.

issues.failure_explanation: For the second matrix function, the proof scales D(z)=alpha z b^T(I-zA)^{-1} by alpha defined from sup ||b^T(I-zA)^{-1}||, omitting the factor z. That does not prove ||D(z)||<=1 on C^-, so Nevanlinna's hypothesis is not verified for the (b^T x Z)(I-A x Z)^{-1} bound. The needed finite constant is instead sup ||z b^T(I-zA)^{-1}||, which is exactly what AS-stability provides.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define alpha^{-1}=sup_{z in C^-} || z b^T (I-zA)^{-1} || for the second application of Nevanlinna; the first inverse bound already follows from ASI-stability.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the uniform-in-Z bound on (b^T x Z)(I-A x Z)^{-1} used in the dy local-error recursion is not established; thm:LTE's uniform LTE expansion is unsupported until this normalization is corrected.
issues.title: Wrong normalization in the second Nevanlinna application for the AS-stability matrix bound
issues.why_classification: The conclusion of the lemma is unchanged and the repair is a one-line normalization directly forced by the AS-stability hypothesis.

issues.failure_explanation: In the induction step for v[i+1], the recursion supplies the forcing a_i, while the lone (i+1)-vertex bushy tree is [root^i] with phi=a_i and coefficient 1. The proof instead adds a[i+1] as phi([root^{i+1}]), a tree with i+2 vertices, and invokes comcoef([root^{i+1}])=1 although Eq:SigmaFormula only defines comcoef through scalvar_{ell,k} for k>=1. The lemma statement is consistent; the induction argument as printed is not.

failure_location.quote: The term $\ac[i+1]$ in \cref{eq:sum2} then adds the missing lone tree to the sum (since $\comcoef([\treeroot^{i+1}]) = 1$)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the induction step replace a[i+1] and [root^{i+1}] by a[i] and [root^i], and state comcoef([root^ell])=1 for the k=0 bushy case.
issues.overall_effect: The combinatorial lemma's proof is invalid at the final induction inclusion, but the stated representation eq:abstractsol and the formulas Eq:PhiFormula/Eq:SigmaFormula remain correct after the index is repaired.
issues.title: Off-by-one forcing term and undefined k=0 combinatorial factor in the abstract tree recursion proof
issues.why_classification: A short local index repair restores the proof without changing the lemma, its coefficients, or any downstream tree expansion.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof says the psi expansion follows by applying lem:abstractrec to dy[0][i] with bimap containing (A C^ell). But the displayed recursion eq:LTE_coeffs:y has no A factor in the nonlinear dy term, and dg[0] is built from the stage errors dY[0]; thus the correct tree map uses the stage functions psi^* of the subtrees, not psi itself. Applied literally, lem:abstractrec would generate a different expression with an extra A in every non-bushy tree.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove eq:LTE_tree_series:y by induction on tree size jointly with the psi^* expansion: substitute Eq:BasisPsi for each psi^*_{tau_j}, use Eq:KroneckerIdentity/Eq:GPsiSum and Eq:MatExpansion inside the recursive definition eq:LTE_tree:psi, and carry the same zeta coefficients from eq:comb1; do not recast dy[1][i] as a self-contained abstract recursion with an extra A.
issues.overall_effect: The tree representation of dy[1] in eq:LTE_tree_series:y is not proved by the displayed 'similarly' step. The Main Result thm:added-1 and the superconvergence part of thm:convergence use these psi functions, so their proofs rely on a repair of this expansion argument.
issues.title: Invalid abstract-recursion derivation of the dy tree expansion: extra A factor and wrong subtree arguments
issues.why_classification: The stated formulas are correct and no global architecture is lost, but the dy tree expansion needs a contained separate induction rather than the claimed direct application of lem:abstractrec.
